claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered BCC solid solution.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of 1719 MPa.
The high Mo content limits plasticity by increasing electronegativity differences and impeding dislocation mobility.
Twenty percent substitution of the Mo sublattice by V produces NbZrTiHf(Mo0.8V0.2).
Partial replacement of Mo by V will lower the alloy's overall electronegativity difference.
NbZrTiHf(Mo0.8V0.2) will retain a disordered single BCC phase.
As-cast processing without heat treatment will preserve the disordered BCC structure.
Lower electronegativity difference will decrease bond-strength heterogeneity.
Decreased bond-strength heterogeneity will promote more uniform dislocation motion.
More uniform dislocation motion will enhance plastic deformation.
Solid-solution strengthening from the constituent elements will largely maintain the alloy's yield strength after V substitution.
The modified alloy will exhibit at least a 5–10% relative improvement in plastic strain or ductility.
The modified alloy will retain a compressive yield strength near 1700 MPa.
Changing elemental composition can alter or stabilize the phase constitution of a multicomponent alloy.
V substitution above approximately 20% may destabilize the BCC phase or induce unwanted second phases in NbZrTiHf(Mo,V).
The hypothesis can be tested by comparing identically processed base and V-modified alloys using room-temperature compression, XRD, TEM, and composition analysis.
The hypothesis is falsified if the modified alloy loses more than 10% of the baseline yield strength, shows no plasticity improvement, or develops phase segregation.

contradictions.description: The phrase 'replace approximately 20 atomic percent of Mo' is quantitatively ambiguous. The formula NbZrTiHf(Mo0.8V0.2) replaces 20% of the Mo sublattice, corresponding to only 4 at.% V in the full alloy, whereas replacing 20 at.% of the full alloy would replace all of the original Mo. The boundary uses the same unresolved '20 atomic percent' wording.
